text:
maya: FYI customer 'NovaHealth' just opened a ticket — they have a corporate outbound proxy + strict allowlist. They need exact IPs and proxy auth guidance ASAP.
sam: Do they want IPs only or hostname-based allowlist? many corp proxies prefer hostnames but most customers do IP allowlists.
maya: They said their firewall only supports IP ranges. Also the proxy requires a per-service token in the Proxy-Authorization header (not basic auth).
liam: Oof. Token-in-proxy is annoying because many proxies terminate TLS and rewrite SNI. If they terminate we can't rely on SNI-based host allowlist.
priya: Ask them if the proxy supports HTTP CONNECT passthrough for outbound TLS. If CONNECT works we can preserve SNI and cert chain.
maya: They said CONNECT is allowed but proxy injects a custom header for auth and strips Authorization on CONNECT sometimes.
sam: Can we give them a tiny curl snippet they can run to test? Also need to send our current egress IP set and a fallback plan.
maya: Yes. Proposed advice to customer (short):
- Allowlist our hosted egress CIDR: 54.210.32.0/22, 34.198.0.0/20 (these are example ranges for the thread)
- Configure proxy to allow HTTP CONNECT to api.redwood-inference.example.com:443 and to forward Proxy-Authorization as-is
- If proxy terminates TLS, configure it to passthrough traffic for api.redwood-inference.example.com or whitelist the hostname in SNI passthrough
- If proxy cannot preserve headers on CONNECT, provide them an outbound nat/static IP option (Dedicated) or a token-based outbound hostname they can allowlist

curl test examples:

```
# test with proxy + proxy auth header
curl -v -x http://proxy.corp:8080 \
  -H "Proxy-Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  https://api.redwood-inference.example.com/v1/health
```

# direct SNI test (bypasses proxy if possible):
```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.example.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.example.com
```

liam: Also mention SNAT/port exhaustion — if they NAT many client IPs behind single SNAT we might see connection resets during bursts. Suggest increasing ephemeral port range and TCP TIME_WAIT tuning on their firewall if they see errors.
priya: For the allowlist doc, we should include a short troubleshooting checklist: 1) can you CONNECT through proxy? 2) does CONNECT preserve Proxy-Authorization? 3) does TLS inspection rewrite SNI? 4) are there SNAT port exhaustion signs?
maya: I'll draft a short customer-facing note and include the curl/openssl checks + list of IPs. We should also add an internal note: if customer can't or won't change proxy behavior, offer Dedicated with static egress IPs (and document SLA/cost).
infra-bot: Reminder — hosted egress CIDRs are rotated weekly. Please include timeframe note: "published ranges are valid for 7 days; we'll notify 72h before change." :information_source:
sam: Can we offer a TLS-terminated, token-auth endpoint at a single stable hostname that accepts Proxy-Authorization in an HTTP header pre-flight? Might be a product ask.
liam: That's a product/infra change. For now, offer the two paths: 1) make proxy passthroughable 2) move them to Dedicated/static-egress.
maya: Ok, I'll post the customer note and attach the quick test steps. tagging @priya and @liam for review. Thanks :thumbsup:
